messages:
maria_g: FYI customer 'BrightDocs' on dedicated eu-2 getting persistent 429s and 500ms+ tail latency since 09:12 UTC after they migrated plan. Ticket INC-54321, customer is blocked for parts of their batch workload.
oscar_sre: Looking at infra now. Which pool exactly? eu-2-dedicated-prod?
maria_g: yes, eu-2-dedicated-prod. Errors started right after their plan switch at ~09:10-09:12.
devin_support: Customer attached traces and sample req_ids (req=bd-9f2a). x-tenant-id=brightdocs. Sending to thread.
oscar_sre: @ops-bot run rate-limiter-stats --tenant brightdocs --pool eu-2-dedicated-prod --window 10m
ops-bot: rate-limiter-stats result: window=10m tenant=brightdocs pool=eu-2-dedicated-prod configured_cap=100 req_units/s avg_in=8000 req_units/s spike=12k tokens_per_req_config=1 observed_tokens_header=100 \nops-bot: Note: detected header->unit mismatch: incoming header 'x-estimated-tokens'=100 treated as 100 req_units each.
raj_eng: That smells like a unit mapping bug — SDK is sending estimated token count but our limiter treats that header as request unit multiplier.
kevin_oncall: Autoscaler logs? If they're doing 8k req_units/s the pool should scale or evict noisy tenant.
oscar_sre: autoscaler didn't scale. I see label reserved:quiet on this pool since last config push; policy prevents scale beyond base_capacity.
maria_g: Customer says they switched from shared to dedicated and their client lib uses header 'x-estimated-tokens' with sdk-v1. They expect tokens->cost, not tokens->request-units.
devin_support: Repro steps from customer: curl -H 'x-tenant:brightdocs' -H 'x-estimated-tokens:100' -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' https://eu.redwood/api/generate  -> after ~70-90 requests they see 429s.
oscar_sre: Quick log snippet:
[09:12:14] rate_limiter INFO tenant=brightdocs cap=100 req_units=8000 tokens_hdr=80000 cap_exceeded=true
[09:12:15] autoscaler INFO pool=eu-2-dedicated-prod label=reserved:quiet skip_scale=true
[09:12:16] serve WARN kv_cache miss tenant=brightdocs prefix=abc123\nraj_eng: Proposed fix: change mapping so x-estimated-tokens from sdk-v1 is interpreted as token_count (for billing/units calculation) not as additional req_units multiplier. Will add header-version check.
oscar_sre: Short-term mitigation options: 1) emergency tenant cap override; 2) remove reserved:quiet label to allow autoscale; 3) add temporary token->req_unit clamp. Which do we want?
kevin_oncall: Applied emergency temp_quota_override for tenant brightdocs at 09:25 UTC to 20k req_units/s. Also removed reserved:quiet label from pool to re-enable autoscale at 09:27 UTC. Monitor now.
devin_support: Customer reports 429s dropped to <1% within 5m after override. They still report 95th latency spikes ~400-600ms on bursts.
oscar_sre: Latency spikes correlate with KV cache misses during burst observed in logs. I can enable tenant prefix caching to reduce tail latency; will coordinate a controlled change.
raj_eng: I'll open PR for rate-limiter header handling and include a migration flag so older SDKs keep current behavior until we flip. Target Canary deploy @10:30 UTC.
maria_g: Thanks all — customer is thanked and copied. Will update INC-54321 with mitigation + timeline.
kevin_oncall: Monitoring for noisy neighbor after override. If other tenants see impact we'll throttle back and open a capacity incident.
oscar_sre: Follow-ups: (1) postmortem on why reserved:quiet label applied automatically in prior deploy; (2) add unit tests for header interpretation; (3) ops runbook update for temp_quota_override steps.
maria_g: Affirmative. Closing interim update, will ping when PR lands.
